items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.
items.title: Voynich Manuscript Final Decoding Procedure

items.summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.
items.title: Phase Organisation Electromagnetic Coupling and Gravitational Receiver Records

items.summary: The onset of ferromagnetic order in one dimension reflects a competition between domain energy and entropy. For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.
items.title: Onset of Ferromagnetic Order in Ising Chains

items.summary: From Reversible Bit-Rings to Quantitative Matter Readouts The Qu Relational Compiler, Three-Dimensional Steric Closure, and Symmetry-Reduced Polymer Mechanics   Driven by Dean A. Kulik October, 2025   1. The Architectural Shift: From State Catalogs to Relational Compilation A foundational problem across discrete mathematics, quantum simulation, and macromolecular physics is distinguishing between a static state catalog and an executable transformation architecture. Conventional computational models treat physical configurations as external data structures submitted to an independent processor: conformations are enumerated in an address table, transitions are assigned by ad hoc hopping matrices or stochastic Monte Carlo rules, and empirical parameters are fitted post hoc to bulk observables. While effective for descriptive curve-fitting, that paradigm divorces the representation of a state from the lawful operations that generate and invert it. Whenever a coarse observation projects away an internal degree of freedom, a state-only model mistakes an observational quotient or a scheduling collision for an absolute physical barrier. The research program consolidated in this report—spanning the native binary partner rings, the One Inverter twisted clock, the Way Between three-dimensional conformational compiler, and the tetrahedral diamond-lattice and polyethylene matter readers through §167—establishes a rigorous alternative: compilation is the continuing resolution of local relational constraints, and physical observables are typed readouts of the resulting operator algebra. Rather than postulating an external machine or assigning arbitrary binary labels to particles, the architecture begins with the minimal condition for a distinction to persist without terminal fixed points ( ) and traces the exact algebraic and geometric structures forced at each scale. This progression unfolds across four interconnected operational tiers that preserve an explicit way home at every scale by pairing a quotient difference reader with a retained frame or phase coordinate. In the first tier, the native binary ring and twisted clock establish divided left and right representative hemispheres and forward/reverse faces governed by fixed-point-free involutions. In the second tier, the planar honeycomb route compiler lifts into a three-dimensional control torus where synchronous bond torsions execute a diagonal bypass around blocked planar corners. In the third tier, three-dimensional tetrahedral chains on the diamond lattice form an unbranched two-sheeted mirror quotient across a central reflection plane. In the fourth tier, the local tetrahedral operations and reflection symmetries collapse the 72-state polyethylene rotational-isomeric-state transfer matrix into four scalar coordinates, resolving the inverse parameter problem via a rank-two observable Jacobian. Across all four tiers, the compiler operates through two governing equations that separate the underlying accumulated transformation from the perspective of a particular observer: In the first equation, local reversible increments —whether bit shifts, modular carries, planar turns, or spatial   bond torsions—accumulate relative to a held reference frame . Changing   reorients the global description rigidly without altering any internal relation , while substituting a subword   with an alternative sequence   having the identical running product produces a strictly local transformation whose exterior remains undisturbed. In the second equation, the multiplicity structure   belongs to the object's own relation complex, while a chosen reader   exposes only the projection . An apparent zero in   or a rank deficiency in a planar Jacobian does not imply the absence of a physical continuation; it diagnoses a specific mismatch between the active transformation and the reader's coordinate chart. Every result included in this synth
items.title: From Reversible Bit-Rings to Quantitative Matter Readouts

items.summary: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described earlier in two articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a statement of conjunctions of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations, inverting the problem by \emph{multiplying} letters (literals) in the transferred clauses, now phrases: $pqrs\cdots s_{\ell}$, and using a binary iterated composition based on \emph{adding polynomials} for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value $1\mapsto 0$(T). To find a solution, we look for repeating literals in the clauses to factor out. With reversed literal repetition, we can even reduce the CNF to the sum of the transformed clauses.
items.title: A Study in Solution Models for SAT using the PBNF-transform

items.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.
items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.
items.title: Phase Compatibility: Harmonic Combination, Selective Participation, Whole Formation, and Recursive Organisation

items.summary: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced. Project website: https://rangenav.github.io/.
items.title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation

items.summary: National methane inventories increasingly rely on satellite-constrained plume inversion, yet the placement of a fixed sensor budget across a landscape of sparse satellite revisits determines how much of the resulting emission-attribution error is reducible and how much is structural. the present analysis formalises budget-constrained sensor placement as a submodular maximisation problem over a plume-inversion error functional, derives a greedy placement rule with a (1 - 1/e) approximation guarantee under a monotone submodular surrogate, and characterises the conditions under which the surrogate diverges from the true attribution error. The analysis is methodological and theoretical: no field deployment is reported. A worked evaluation on a computed plume field calibrated to published satellite revisit statistics shows that the greedy rule recovers between 71 and 88 per cent of the oracle placement gain across budget levels, while the residual attribution error is dominated by revisit sparsity rather than by sensor count. Inventory audits should report a placement-attributable error component separately from a revisit-attributable component, because conflating the two leads auditors to over-attribute residual uncertainty to instrumentation and under-attribute it to orbital sampling. The contribution is a formal decomposition of emission-attribution error into placement-reducible and revisit-structural parts, together with a placement algorithm whose guarantees are stated relative to that decomposition.
tags: methane plume inversion; sensor placement; submodular optimisation; satellite revisit; emission attr
items.title: Budget-constrained sensor placement for methane plume inversion under sparse satellite revisits: a computer-science evaluation of emission-attribution error in national inventory audits

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine: typed construction search, independent checks and recorded failure residues. This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. The verifier reconstructs facets, primal and polar lattice points, strict containment, interval costs, pair bounds and exceptional-census coverage. It does not reconstruct the entire classification histogram. The sharp seed constant, Hodge F2/F3-prime, GSC and the continuum Yang–Mills problem remain open. The full four-target closure benchmark has not been crossed. Graph survivors are necessary candidate configurations, not constructed semiregular objects. No new Lean formalization of the interval refinement is claimed.

The archive contains the pre-registered canonical fit (v1.0), the frozen v1.1 analysis (angular torque test; joint fit with mixed noise), a reproduction on separate hardware, a second-algorithm check, and frozen acceptance tolerances for a future independent fitter. items.summary: In standard acoustic anomaly detection (ASD), models are usually trained separately for each machine or domain using explicit metadata. However, in realistic deployments, machine identifiers are incomplete, unreliable, or simply unavailable. Thus, metadata-free machinery ASD asks a single model to monitor mixed machine populations without machine IDs. In this paper, we argue that the main failure mode is not a weak detector family, but representation entanglement. The heterogeneous normal modes overlap in frozen pre-trained feature spaces, making anomaly scoring and approximate retrieval unreliable. We study this problem directly and propose HARMONY (Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source acoustic aNomalY detection), an anchor-guided geometric repartitioning framework that reorganizes mixed-source features into compact Voronoi regions and reuses this structure for hierarchical retrieval. On DCASE 2020, HARMONY improves mean AUC from 75.40% to 90.00% (14.60 percentage points) over the strongest unified baseline and from 83.90% to 90.00% over a strong foundation-feature baseline. On a single CPU, its hierarchical retrieval achieves a 7.8x speedup over exhaustive search with only a 0.20 percentage-point AUC drop. These results suggest that incorporating explicit geometric partitioning can improve both detection accuracy and retrieval efficiency for ASD. Code is available at https://github.com/Zzyh0208/HARMONY.
items.title: HARMONY: Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source Machinery Acoustic Anomaly Detection

items.summary: RFT-FaultBench provides training-process telemetry for anomaly detection and failure-type diagnosis in reinforcement fine-tuning. This revised dataset contains 2,630 runs (339 normal and 2,291 injected), 72,100 train-step records, and 2,617,600 training trajectories across OpenRLHF, AgentEvolver, and TRL and five task categories: arithmetic reasoning, GSM8K-style mathematical reasoning, code generation, verifiable instruction following, and tool calling. It includes 55 compound-failure runs for detection; diagnosis uses 2,236 single-failure runs. Task versions and native failure-label coverage differ across frameworks. The package includes run-level artifacts, canonical labels and seeds, five seed-grouped evaluation folds, 25 one-shot support draws, provenance and exclusion ledgers, per-file checksums, and Python example loaders and validation tools. Membership follows the frozen 2026-10-12 evaluation snapshot. It updates the earlier 779-run release; no new training was performed during packaging. GitHub companion: AIOps4LLM/RFT-FaultBench . Related manuscript: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Diagnosis for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning. Extract RFT-FaultBench-full.tar.gz and consult its README and docs for schemas, verification evidence, and evaluation scope. The dataset continues the CC BY 4.0 license of the preceding Zenodo version.
items.title: RFT-FaultBench-full

items.summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
items.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

items.summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.
tags: censored regression; intermediate efficiency; long-range dependence; random field; randomization tes
items.title: Intermediate efficiency of censored regression tests on stationary random fields

items.summary: Differential Privacy (DP) has become a prominent approach for protecting graph data releases, yet empirical auditing methodologies have largely been developed for tabular datasets and machine learning pipelines rather than graph-structured outputs. We present a methodology for empirically auditing DP graph release mechanisms, identifying two graph-specific audit design problems: canary construction and witness statistic selection. We combine these components with an established statistically certified testing procedure and implement the resulting methodology as an open-source Python toolkit. To demonstrate the approach, we audit a published state-of-the-art Node-DP graph release mechanism. Across a series of synthetic and real-world canary pairs, we obtain certified lower bounds on the privacy parameter {\varepsilon} that exceed the claimed value, yielding counterexamples sufficient to falsify the claimed guarantee for the audited implementation. The violations persist under progressively stronger restrictions on the input domain, including non-empty and connected graphs. We also show that witness selection can materially affect whether a violation is detected, highlighting the importance of evaluating a diverse battery of statistics when auditing DP graph release mechanisms.
items.title: Practical Auditing of Differentially Private Graph Release Mechanisms: Methodology, Toolkit, and Case Study

Its prespecified composite fidelity endpoint had 0/480 base failures; the exact one-sided 95% upper failure bound was 0.622167%, with exact p=0.00803329 at a 1% null failure rate. Earlier 40-bit stress failures remain valid. Signed integrate-and-fire packets operate within a numerical host-recursive Gaussian-process mixture tracker. Host gains, weights, mixture assembly and forecast algebra remain numerical. Author code is MIT; retained third-party components keep their notices. The original pipeline retains frozen path/dependency assumptions and is not claimed fully relocatable; the portable verifier checks the saved S5 evidence without importing that pipeline. Original locks, analyses, stress breaches and failed endpoints are retained. The independent-machine R1 replay remains not passed (7/8). S5 is fresh synthetic confirmation, not another independent-machine replay. Cross-platform regeneration previously agreed within 5e-11 rather than bitwise; saved synthetic inputs remain the numerical reference. External-data exclusions are unchanged: no K-Radar data/derived outcomes, TartanAviation raw archives, recorded aircraft coordinates, recorded input/truth arrays or recorded forecast means are redistributed. The new S5 positions, truth and compact forecasts are wholly synthetic. Full component and internal-state traces remain local for size; original hashes are retained. Mixed-data manuscript snapshots and edit specifications are excluded. Provider data must be obtained from official sources under their terms. No neuromorphic hardware energy, latency or efficiency benefit is claimed. No external funding; no competing interests. Files remain restricted for peer review. The manuscript remains under author review; this archive is not journal submission.

Release m3-v1.0.0, promoted without scientific changes from independently verified m3-v1.0.0-rc3. The canonical TAR contains 38,186 files, 3,898,019,840 bytes; SHA-256 dafaa0df527176a9c54e0c40f5e5e4d59cebbce052c034e4df4f0f5cd5278f89. Original provider traces are excluded. Frozen preparation-time metadata inside the immutable archive records its provenance and does not describe current public availability. Public companion records: curated source https://github.com/SoroushVahidi/llm-serving-scheduler-robustness-benchmark/releases/tag/m3-v1.0.0; authoritative result-table dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/SoroushVahidi/llm-serving-common-contract-m3; Kaggle mirror https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/soroushvahidi/llm-serving-common-contract-m3. The table mirrors contain identical underlying result data and are not independent experiments. The separate older LSSP release is not overwritten.
items.title: Scheduler Equivalence and Performance Trade-offs under a Common LLM-Serving Contract — Complete Reproducibility Artifact — m3-v1.0.0

items.summary: Background : The rapid digitisation of allied health education has led to an alarming rise in Digital Eye Strain (DES), also termed Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS), among undergraduate Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) students. Standard therapies like artificial tears provide temporary lubrication without resolving the underlying neuro-vascular tension and oxidative ocular stress. Objectives : To evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy of daily Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash over 4 weeks on digital asthenopia, tear film stability, tear volume, and visual comfort in a cohort of 16 BPT students. Methodology : A 4-week prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled empirical pilot trial was conducted at Maya Devi University, Dehradun. Sixteen BPT students (aged 18–25) meeting inclusion criteria (screen time ≥ 6 hrs/day, CVS-Q ≥ 6, TBUT < 10 s) were randomized 1:1 into Group A (Jal Neti, n=8) and Group B (Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash, n=8). Outcome metrics assessed at baseline (Day 0) and post-intervention (Day 28) included: Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q), Visual Fatigue Scale (VFS, 0-60), Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT, seconds), and Schirmer’s Test-I (mm/5 min). Results : Both groups exhibited statistically significant intra-group improvements across all parameters (p < 0.001). Group B (Triphala) achieved superior improvement in tear film stability and lacrimal secretion: TBUT increased by +4.15 ± 0.80 s in Group B vs. +2.30 ± 0.60 s in Group A (p < 0.001); Schirmer-I values increased by +4.85 ± 1.10 mm in Group B vs. +2.65 ± 0.85 mm in Group A (p < 0.001). Conversely, Group A (Jal Neti) achieved greater relief from central visual fatigue and periocular headaches: VFS scores decreased by -18.60 ± 2.95 points in Group A vs. -14.25 ± 2.75 points in Group B (p < 0.01). Total CVS-Q scores dropped markedly in both groups (Group A: 12.75 to 5.25; Group B: 13.00 to 4.90). Conclusion : Both modalities significantly alleviate digital eye strain in BPT students. Sterile Triphala eye wash is particularly potent for restoring ocular surface hydration and tear film stability, whereas Jal Neti excels in alleviating deep neuromuscular fatigue and periorbital strain.
tags: Digital Eye Strain, Jal Neti, Triphala, Tear Break-Up Time, Schirmer's Test, Physiotherapy Students,
items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash on Digital Asthenopia, Tear Film Dynamics, and Visual Comfort in Undergraduate Physiotherapy Students: A Single-Center Empirical Pilot Study

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.
items.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination

items.summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
items.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

items.summary: Analysis code for the manuscript submitted to Kidney International Reports (KIR-S-26-00587). The study uses target trial emulation with clone-censor-weighting (CCW) to estimate the effect of early (<=24 h) vs no/late insulin initiation on AKI progression among sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) patients, stratified by a glucose-trajectory phenotype (P2 = high-sustained). Includes primary CCW analyses, a negative control outcome (NCO) sensitivity analysis, eICU-CRD 2.0 external validation (phenotypic portability), and an exploratory MIMIC-III CareVue replication. Data sources (PhysioNet credentialed): MIMIC-IV (discovery), eICU-CRD 2.0, MIMIC-III CareVue. Reported under STROBE + RECORD + TARGET.
items.title: BD2: Insulin timing and glucose-trajectory phenotypes in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury - analysis code

items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
items.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

items.summary: Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. We instead develop OPTIC (Output-Path-fitted, Token-shared Indexed Codes), which stores one quantized code tuple per token and decodes it at every layer with a layer-specific affine decoder. Codes and decoders are fitted to the PLE output path rather than to the stored vectors. At about $100\times$ PLE compression of bfloat16 (BF16) E4B, OPTIC retains an aggregate 97.8% of the uncompressed model's performance across seven benchmarks, whereas product quantization, the strongest of six conventional baselines, retains 66.3%. At $594\times$ and $1,002\times$ PLE compression of BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 90.5% and 84.1%. On the official E4B release with 4-bit linear weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16), OPTIC retains 96.9% at about $100\times$ PLE compression. During inference at about $100\times$ PLE compression, BF16 E4B uses 29.7% less GPU memory than with uncompressed PLE at the same key-value cache size, while running at most 0.40% slower.
items.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

items.summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
items.title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0

items.summary: EnzyPair is a benchmark dataset for evaluating enzyme-function similarity at low sequence identity. It contains 1,664 same-EC4 protein pairs and 4,992 structure-matched different-EC4 controls involving 2,465 proteins. The release includes protein sequences, EC annotations, TM-align measurements, residue alignments, exclusion records, source provenance and software versions.
items.title: EnzyPair: a dataset of same-function enzyme pairs with structure-matched controls at low sequence identity

items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

items.summary: Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.
items.title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning

items.summary: Unlike conventional GUI agents, personalized GUI agents require user preferences to guide sequential execution over changing GUI states. This raises two challenges: determining HOW each preference should alter execution strategy and WHEN it should take effect along the interaction trajectory. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate overall task success, offering limited insight into these questions. We introduce PrefDiag-Bench with two components: (1) a categorization of preferences into five types, characterizing HOW they affect execution; and (2) a stage-wise diagnostic framework with 1,664 probes, tracing WHEN preferences should take effect and where failures occur. We evaluate eleven GUI agent systems, including end-to-end agents and agentic workflows, under two forms of user context: explicit user profiles and behavioral memory logs. Although existing agents achieve relatively high completion rates on non-personalized tasks, performance is substantially lower on preference-personalized tasks. Even the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves only 47.17% on Process preferences under explicit user profiles. Agents struggle particularly with Ranking and Process preferences. Further analysis reveals two key capability bottlenecks: selecting relevant evidence from user history and recognizing when preferences should take effect during execution. Controlled interventions that explicitly provide relevant evidence improve end-to-end task success by up to 7.06%. PrefDiag-Bench offers a more systematic evaluation of GUI agents' personalization capabilities beyond overall task success. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Zhixin-L/PrefDiag-Bench.
items.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents

items.summary: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) leverages centralized knowledge graphs to enhance large language models with structured knowledge retrieval. However, real-world knowledge is inherently distributed across multiple organizations rather than being centrally accessible. Privacy constraints further prohibit sharing entire local knowledge graphs, preventing GraphRAG from effectively retrieving and utilizing distributed knowledge. To this end, we propose Federated GraphRAG (FedGRAG), a unified framework for distributed graph retrieval and knowledge-enhanced generation over multiple clients with knowledge graphs. Specifically, we address two fundamental challenges in federated GraphRAG. First, the absence of a global knowledge graph makes unified retrieval impossible. To address this, we develop a Federated Knowledge Routing mechanism that efficiently identifies relevant clients through lightweight knowledge indices without exposing local graph structures. Second, local graph memory cannot be shared directly because it contains sensitive entities and knowledge information. We therefore propose a controlled-disclosure evidence construction method. It extracts retrieved evidence subgraphs and converts them into an evidence abstract, enabling evidence conversion and reconstruction on the server. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Federated GraphRAG consistently outperforms existing baselines in both retrieval and downstream generation tasks, establishing a new paradigm for deploying GraphRAG in federated environments.
items.title: Federated Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

items.summary: Processed single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data for “Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics” This record contains processed sequencing data, derived analysis objects, and analysis code supporting the transcriptomic analyses in Sun, Ogishi, Barrett, Jiang, Yan et al., Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics . The study repurposes the helminth-derived TGF-β mimic TGM1 as a cell-type-targeted immunosuppressant by replacing its CD44-binding domains 4–5 with high-affinity targeting modules. Constructs targeting mouse or human CD4 or CD8α, or human CD19, are designed to preferentially deliver TGF-β receptor agonism to selected lymphocyte subsets. Two datasets are included, each as a separate archive. 1. Single-cell RNA-seq of B-cell-enriched samples from human spleen organoids (raw reads: GEO GSE346912). Human spleen organoids from two deceased organ donors (Sp88, 33-year-old female; Sp99, 53-year-old male) were stimulated with live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) in the presence of vehicle, untargeted low-affinity TGM1 (domains 1–3), or the CD19-targeted TGF-β agonist TGM1-hCD19, alongside unstimulated controls (4 conditions × 2 donors = 8 samples). On day 7, B cells were enriched by negative selection, captured on a 10x Genomics Chromium X instrument using Single Cell 5′ R2-only v3 chemistry, and sequenced as paired-end 150-bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Reads were aligned to GRCh38-2024-A and quantified with Cell Ranger v9.0.1, with intronic reads included, recovering approximately 14,000–27,000 cells per sample. After quality control in Seurat v5.3.1, 163,632 cells were retained (33,179 mock; 51,696 LAIV; 43,858 LAIV + untargeted TGM1; 34,899 LAIV + TGM1-hCD19), of which 130,987 were B-lineage cells. Cell-type annotation combined Louvain clustering, label transfer from the Human Tonsil Atlas v2 ( https://zenodo.org/records/8373756 ), and manual curation using canonical markers. The record provides Cell Ranger filtered feature-barcode matrices and per-sample QC summaries; cell-type label-transfer and curated annotation tables; differential expression and fgsea results; pySCENIC v0.12.1 regulon activity matrices (265 regulons, including IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1); velocyto loom files and scVelo per-cell velocity outputs underlying the RNA velocity analysis; gene signature and cell-cycle scores; and all R and Python analysis code. These analyses support suppression of the germinal center B-cell–to–plasmablast transition by B-cell-targeted TGF-β agonism, with markedly reduced plasmablast and plasma-cell representation, increased naïve B-cell representation, and IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1 regulon activities approaching unstimulated levels. RNA velocity analyses are consistent with reduced progression through the plasmablast differentiation trajectory. 2. Bulk RNA-seq of antigen-specific mouse CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells (raw reads: GEO GSE346305). Naïve Thy1.1⁺ OT-II (CD4⁺) and OT-I (CD8⁺) T cells were co-transferred into Thy1.1⁻ recipient mice, which were then immunized with ovalbumin emulsified in complete Freund’s adjuvant and treated every other day with PBS, untargeted TGM1, TGM1-mCD4, or TGM1-mCD8 (approximately 40–50 pmol per dose for TGM1 constructs). Donor OT-II and OT-I cells were sorted from draining lymph nodes for RNA sequencing. Naïve OT-II and OT-I cells were included as baseline controls, yielding 20 libraries in total (2 cell types × 5 conditions, comprising 4 treatment groups and 1 naïve control group, × 2 biological replicates). Reads were aligned to mm10 with Rsubread v2.18.0, quantified with featureCounts, and analyzed with DESeq2. Downstream analyses include principal component analysis (PCA) of variance-stabilized counts, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) against Hallmark gene sets, and exploratory immune-cell deconvolution using EPIC with the Monaco ref
items.title: Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics

items.summary: Ray tracing (RT) generates photorealistic images by simulating the physical behavior of light as it interacts with surfaces in a virtual scene. In film production and high-end rendering pipelines, this technique computes global illumination, reflections, refractions, and soft shadows by tracing millions of light rays per frame and accurately modeling their bounces and attenuation. Contemporary GPUs incorporate specialized ray tracing hardware to accelerate key operations in the traversal pipeline. By accelerating these stages in hardware, the unit enables real-time ray tracing for complex scenes that previously required offline computation. However, ray tracing introduces substantial control and data divergence. Each ray may traverse a different set of nodes in the acceleration structure, encounter distinct materials, or terminate at varying depths. This irregularity reduces thread coherence and exposes a fundamental disparity between the GPU SIMT and per-thread execution model of dedicated RT units, where each ray progresses independently. In this work, we seek to validate assumptions made in open-source infrastructure and identify potential inefficiencies in resource management within the ray tracing pipeline. To address inefficiency caused by mismatches between SIMT and RT granularities, we propose Ray-by-Ray, which decomposes on-chip buffers into the granularity of individual rays and introduces lightweight management structures that enable more warps to run in parallel without increasing buffer capacity. This approach improves ray tracing unit utilization and increases memory-level parallelism. Experimental results show that Ray-by-Ray achieves an average performance improvement of 1.91x over the baseline, with an area overhead of 0.19\%.
items.title: Ray-by-Ray: Fine-Grained Resource Management for GPU Ray Tracing Units

items.summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervent
items.title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine: typed construction search, independent checks and recorded failure residues. This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. The verifier reconstructs facets, primal and polar lattice points, strict containment, interval costs, pair bounds and exceptional-census coverage. It does not reconstruct the entire classification histogram. The sharp seed constant, Hodge F2/F3-prime, GSC and the continuum Yang–Mills problem remain open. The full four-target closure benchmark has not been crossed. Graph survivors are necessary candidate configurations, not constructed semiregular objects. No new Lean formalization of the interval refinement is claimed.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: Biomimetic design often risks superficial imitation and functional greenwashing. We introduce the Illusion-Real Biomimicry Index (IRBI), a non-compensatory composite metric bridging the Double Diamond design process. The IRBI synthesizes an evidence-anchored claim ledger (Illusion Index Framework, IIF) with a multi-criteria systemic quality framework (Integrated Biomimicry Impact Evaluation Framework, IBIEF) via a weighted geometric mean equipped with a Heaviside veto trigger. The methodology is evaluated across two tracks. Part A assesses three engineering artefacts (an industrial symbiosis network, a passive sharkskin foil, and an archetypal imitation) under a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis over claim measurement uncertainties, AHP weights, and provisional veto thresholds. Part B explores the feasibility of extracting dynamic stability indicators from inertial sensor time series during controlled movements (cervical kinematics, N=1 ). Part A yielded deterministic IRBI scores of 0.90, 0.62, and 0.00 (veto triggered), respectively, demonstrating 100% hierarchical rank preservation. In Part B, amplitude-distribution entropy asymmetry captured postural uncoupling, whereas the Rosenstein Lyapunov slope failed to reject the linearly correlated noise null hypothesis. The IRBI provides a mathematically auditable gatekeeper against greenwashing, while dynamic indicator telemetry requires multi-subject cohort calibration before certification deployment.
items.title: Biomimicry or Greenwashing? Operationalizing Authenticity via Non-Linear Dynamics

items.summary: Code and results for the paper “Learning Interpretable Dispatch Rules for Aircraft Disassembly under Disruption” (H. Saleh, submitted). The package contains: an event-driven simulator of aircraft teardown with licensed crews, zone capacity and mass balance; two disruption models, one with announced absences and one with pause-and-resume absences, both with hidden work; an independent schedule checker and the hindsight lower bound; genetic programming for priority rules; the competitors: classic priority rules, a look-ahead (rollout), and CP-SAT re-planning at every event; the result files of every experiment in the paper (15,734 schedules, all valid), with scripts that rebuild the tables and figures from them. The learned rule is priority = LST − 0.5·CERT: the latest start time minus a head start for licensed seats. Benchmark data are not included. The aircraft disassembly benchmark of Thomas and Schaus and the MSLIB instances are downloaded from their sources; the README gives the commands and pinned versions. Code: MIT license. Results and figures: CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Learned dispatch rules for aircraft disassembly under disruption: code and results
